name: Minneapolis–St. Paul
lede: One of the best disc golf metros in America — Blue Ribbon Pines, Bryant Lake, Kaposia, and the deep bench behind them. We're publishing the Twin Cities' best first.
introParagraphs: The Twin Cities are a top-three disc golf metro in the country, and the top tier shows it. Blue Ribbon Pines in East Bethel is the crown jewel — 27 holes of open-and-wooded design with ponds and doglegs, a pro shop, and a reputation that draws players from across the region. Bryant Lake in Eden Prairie is the scenic technical test with the lake views.

Kaposia in South St. Paul is the 27-hole championship course, Lakewood Hills is the friendly rolling-hills favorite, and Acorn in Roseville rounds out the published five with its dual-tee, dual-basket variety. The destination courses are pay to play; the rest are free.
New here? Lakewood Hills to learn, Blue Ribbon for the full experience.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Twin Cities metro?
faqs.answer: Around 60 courses across the metro — one of the deepest markets in the country. We're publishing the best first — 5 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in the Twin Cities?
faqs.answer: Blue Ribbon Pines in East Bethel — the 27-hole crown jewel with ponds, doglegs, and a pro shop. Bryant Lake is the scenic runner-up.

faqs.question: Are the Twin Cities' disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: It's a mix — Lakewood Hills and Acorn are free, while the destination courses are pay to play (Blue Ribbon $8, Bryant Lake $10, Kaposia $5).

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in the Twin Cities?
faqs.answer: Lakewood Hills in White Bear Lake — friendly rolling hills with dual tees on most holes. Acorn in Roseville is another approachable option.
